notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
WHOIS queries the domain registration database for: registrant contact, administrative/technical contacts, registrar, name servers, creation/expiration dates, and transfer lock status. Passive technique — no traffic to target.

=== INTEL VALUE ===
Registrant name/email/phone: social engineering targets, phishing contact list. Name servers: AXFR attempt targets (especially if internally managed vs third-party). Registration date: domain age (legitimacy indicator). Expiration date: upcoming expiration = domain hijacking research. clientProhibited/serverProhibited statuses: transfer lock indicators.

=== LIMITATIONS ===
GDPR compliance and privacy proxy services (WhoisGuard, Domains By Proxy) redact registrant data for European targets and privacy-conscious registrants. Many records now show "REDACTED FOR PRIVACY" or proxy email addresses.

=== HISTORICAL WHOIS ===
Services like WhoisFreaks provide historical records showing ownership changes, contact changes, and infrastructure evolution over time — useful for threat intelligence and tracking acquisition patterns.
